data.name: Mahanthesh
data.gender_notes: Mahanthesh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is the great master or lord over a particular subject, place or people. The name Mahanthesh carries the meaning “Great Lord” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Mahanthesh usually hope their child will grow to embody great lord and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A title given to spiritual or religious leaders in Hinduism
data.etymology: Mahanthesh belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Great Lord.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mahanthesh total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Mahanthesh" highlights the cultural significance of hereditary spiritual leaders in Hindu society. These leaders, often referred to as sadhus or mahants, hold a respected position within their communities due to their deep knowledge and dedication to spiritual practices. The suffix "Mahant" emphasizes the greatness and authority of such individuals, conveying their esteemed social status and influence.
data.spiritual_significance: Mahanthesh may also indicate a celibate religious leader who has devoted their entire life to serving their deity or God. The name signifies the individual's commitment, spiritual progress, and enlightenment, symbolizing the inner wisdom and understanding gained through a lifetime of dedication and self-discipline. The name represents the deep connection between the individual and the divine, a testament to the individual's spiritual growth and devotion.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Mahanthesh: Supreme God's Vessel or God in Embodiment. A title given to spiritual leaders who have devoted their lives to serving and representing the divine.
